solution_level.why: Measured: no score-shaped metric separates the arms at 60 steps (held-out 0.0570 vs 0.0592; training reward 0.0161 vs 0.0156). The quantities that do separate them are structural invariants of the advantage tensor, not scores.
solution_level.next_step: Either grade the invariants directly from metrics_*.jsonl (advantages/min must go negative; more than one distinct advantages/max; all pinned steps present), or measure whether a longer budget makes accuracy separate. Both options are written up in readme.md. Do not invent an accuracy threshold from these 60-step numbers.

offline_wandb_artifact.why: This verl tree has no Tracking.finish() call (the sibling task's addition was deliberately not carried over, to keep the diff against upstream equal to the injected defect). The process therefore exits mid-write and run-*.wandb ends on an unterminated FIRST fragment after 501 records, confirmed by walking the datastore framing. A truncated binary is worse than none.
offline_wandb_artifact.next_step: If offline W&B is ever needed, add Tracking.finish() to the control arm only, or sync from a run that exits cleanly. The .jsonl carries the same numbers in full.

oracle_corrections_from_measurement.claim: critic/advantages/mean equals critic/rewards/mean digit for digit
oracle_corrections_from_measurement.measured: advantages/mean is a response-token-weighted masked mean, so it only approximates the sequence-reward mean (step 4: 0.010730 vs 0.015625). Only 27/60 steps matched within 1e-6, and those are the steps where reward was 0.
oracle_corrections_from_measurement.why_it_mattered: An oracle demanding exact equality would have rejected a correct diagnosis.

oracle_corrections_from_measurement.measured: It is exactly 0.9999990463256836 on every rewarded step = fp32 1/(1+1e-6), i.e. reward 1.0 over the substituted id2std=1.0 plus the epsilon guard. Bit-identical across every rewarded step, which is a stronger fingerprint than '1.0'.

oracle_corrections_from_measurement.claim: held-out accuracy fails to improve and entropy falls faster
oracle_corrections_from_measurement.measured: Entropy does fall faster (1.31 vs 2.99). But held-out accuracy RISES over the run (0.0454 -> 0.0570) and is within noise of the control arm (0.0592). The oracle now states plainly that a held-out-curve-based diagnosis has not identified the defect.

The `console` tracking backend prints from inside the TaskRunner Ray actor, and Ray did not forward that actor's stdout to the driver on that run; the numbers existed only in /tmp/ray/session_latest/logs/worker-*.out, which is ephemeral and not part of the task.
